```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(meta)
library(metafor)
library(metadat)
library(haven)
library(writexl)
library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)
options(scipen = 999)
```


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r}
data_purchase <- data.frame()
# filter to a needed dependent variable
data_purchase <- appliances %>% 
                  filter(dep_variable_purchase_category == "purschase (probability) of efficient appliance")
# exclude the outliers
data_purchase <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(z_value < 0.5 & z_value > -0.5 )
```

```{r}
data_purchase_washing <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(washing_machine == 1)

data_purchase_dryer <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(clothes_dryer == 1)

data_purchase_dishwasher <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(dishwasher == 1)

data_purchase_refrigerator <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(refrigerator == 1)

data_purchase_heat_pump <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(heat_pump == 1)

data_purchase_lighting <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(lighting == 1)

data_purchase_water <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(water_heater == 1)

data_purchase_ac <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(ac == 1)

data_purchase_tv <- data_purchase %>% 
                  filter(tv == 1)
```

```{r}
### RANDOM EFFECTS MODEL ###
##washing machine
m.gen_purchase_washing <- metagen(TE = z_value,
                 seTE = z_variance,
                 data = data_purchase_washing,
                 studlab = authors,
                 sm = "ZCOR",
                 fixed = FALSE,
                 random = TRUE,
                 backtransf = F,
                 )

## forest plot of purchase

png(file = "forestplot_washing_random.png", width = 6000, height = 3000, res = 500)
forest.meta(m.gen_purchase_washing,
           leftcols = c("authors", "Intervention"),
           digits =6,
           col.random = "Red",
           xlab = "Effect Sizes",
           col.square = "Blue")

### FIXED EFFECTS MODEL ###
  
m1.gen_purchase_washing <- metagen(TE = z_value,
                 seTE = z_variance,
                 data = data_purchase_washing,
                 studlab = authors,
                 sm = "ZCOR",
                 fixed = TRUE,
                 random = FALSE,
                 backtransf = F,
                 )

## forest plot of purchase

png(file = "forestplot_washing_fixed.png", width = 6000, height = 3000, res = 500)
forest.meta(m1.gen_purchase_washing,
           leftcols = c("authors", "Intervention"),
           digits =6,
           col.random = "Red",
           xlab = "Effect Sizes",
           col.square = "Blue")       
```

```{r}
### MULTI-LEVEL MODEL ###
# convert categorical variables to numeric
# discuss the variables to include

# Step 1: Create a meta-analysis model
meta_model <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase, method = "FE", mods = ~ intervention+0)

# Step 2: Fit the meta-analysis model
meta_result <- rma(z_value, z_variance, data = data_purchase, method = "REML", mods = ~(1 | intervention))

meta_result<-rma.mv(z_value, z_variance, mods = ~  ~ intervention+0, 
                               random = ~ as.factor(sr_no) | as.factor(study_ID), data = appliancespurchase, method = "REML")

# Step 3: Inspect the meta-analysis results
summary(meta_result)

# Step 4: Explore heterogeneity
forest(meta_result)

# Step 5: Conduct subgroup analyses or meta-regression (if applicable)
# Assume you have an additional predictor variable named 'predictor'
meta_model <- rma(z_value, z_variance, mods = ~ appliance +0 , data = data_purchase, method = "REML")
```
